the_signal.headline: Knowledge graphs vs vector RAG: which grounds your revenue agents?
the_signal.body: n8n just published a breakdown of when to use LLM knowledge graphs versus vector RAG for grounding AI workflows. For GTM engineers building agent-based revenue systems, this is the difference between structured entity relationships (better for deal routing, account scoring) and fuzzy semantic search (better for discovery). Pick wrong and your agents hallucinate buyer signals or miss high-intent accounts.

thread_of_day.takeaway: Contract testing catches breaking API changes before they tank your revenue workflows—critical when your lead qualification engine depends on CRM/data warehouse APIs staying stable.

whats_moving.topic: Knowledge graph vs vector RAG clarity
whats_moving.context: GTM teams need to choose the right grounding strategy for their agents—structured data wins for account context, vectors win for content relevance.
Self-hosted workflow engines now have per-execution LLM cost control, enabling GTM teams to scale AI agent usage without surprise bills.

act_on_this: Audit your current lead scoring and routing workflows: if they're built on iPaaS with API deps, map which CRM/data APIs are mission-critical and implement contract testing today before they break in production.
